## Natural history notes

A small wading bird characterized by a dark greenish back, chestnut neck, dark cap, short yellow legs, and a dagger-like bill. In Florida, the Green Heron is found along ponds, lakes, marshes, mangroves, canals, swamps, wooded wetlands, and quiet stream edges where dense shoreline vegetation provides cover. It feeds by stalking or standing still at the water’s edge to catch small fish, frogs, insects, crustaceans, and other aquatic prey, sometimes using bait such as insects or small objects to lure fish within striking distance.
